newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close down on Gulf tensions.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close down on Gulf tensions.

text.p: Taiwan share prices ended down but off their intra-day lows on Wednesday amid concerns of rising tensions in the Gulf after the U.S. military launched a second wave of cruise missile attacks on Iraq.
The weighted index finished down 29.19 points or 0.47 percent at 6,228.78, off a low of 6,197.54. Turnover was a modest T$40.17 billion.
"People are concerned about the development in Iraq," said Tsao Chung-ping of Ting Kong Securities. "They simply do not want to make any moves at the moment," Tsao said.
The market is worried that a prolonged tension in the Middle East may cause rises in domestic oil prices and trigger inflation.
Local media reported that Chinese Petroleum Corp, the island's state oil monopoly, said it had no immediate plan to raise oil prices.
"This is not the second Gulf war. The impact should be short-lived," said Tank Hung of Yuan Ta Securities.
Brokers also noted investors were not eager to dump their stocks and some institutions hunted bargain at low levels.
Blue chip electronics continued to draw active buying despite a weak market as prices for dynamic random access memory chips have rebounded in international markets, brokers said.
Computer giant Acer Inc jumped T$1.4 or 3.66 percent to T$39.7. Macronix gained 90 cents or 2.67 percent to T$34.6.
Construction sector was weak, with the second most active issue, Hung Fu Construction, plunging by the daily seven percent limit to T$36.9.
Overall sentiment would remain cautious in the market. Brokers saw initial support at 6,000-point level.
